findings.summary: pct()'s total==0 guard, and the (0,0) default in c.get('LINE',(0,0))/c.get('BRANCH',(0,0)), are never exercised. Every report() fixture supplies BOTH LINE and BRANCH counters with missed+covered > 0 (checked all 8 call sites: (3,1,3,3), (90,10,100,0), (100,0,80,20), (19,1,9,1), (3,1,3,3), (99,1,95,1), (100,0,100,0)x2 -- none has a zero total, none omits a counter type).
findings.failure_scenario: Mutate pct() to `return 100.0 * covered / total` (drop the zero-guard). All 11 tests still pass, because none constructs a report where a counter type is missing or its total is zero. But this is a realistic, not contrived, production input: JaCoCo omits the BRANCH counter entirely for a class with no branches (a plain record/POJO -- exactly the 'no product code yet' stub the exclusion test itself describes). Verified directly: parsing `<report><counter type="LINE" missed="0" covered="10"/></report>` (no BRANCH counter) through the current code yields branch=100.0 (the zero-guard treats 'nothing to branch on' as full coverage); the mutated pct() raises ZeroDivisionError on the same input. A gate that dies with an uncaught exception on a branch-free module -- likely to be the very first real module this gate runs against -- is caught by nothing in this suite. The inverse mutation (`return 0.0 if total == 0 else ...`, silently failing every branch-free module instead of passing it) is equally invisible.

findings.summary: The module-discovery filter that excludes buildSrc is asserted by no test. Every fixture module() call creates a bare top-level directory (always named "format"); none ever creates a path under `buildSrc/`, so the exclusion clause is dead code as far as this suite can tell.
findings.failure_scenario: Delete `and not p.startswith('buildSrc/')` from the module-discovery comprehension. All 11 CoverageGateTest cases still pass -- none constructs a buildSrc/build.gradle.kts fixture. But this is not a hypothetical: `git ls-files '*/build.gradle.kts'` in THIS repo returns `buildSrc/build.gradle.kts` at exactly one slash, so the unfiltered set genuinely includes 'buildSrc' as a module (verified by running the actual git-ls-files/filter logic against this tree). buildSrc's own build.gradle.kts has no `jacoco {}` block and produces no jacocoTestReport.xml, but it does compile test classes -- so with the filter removed, check-coverage.sh would classify buildSrc as 'has classes, no report' and FAIL on every single commit, including a docs-only one. That is the gate-fails-for-the-wrong-reason class this review round is explicitly watching for ("a gate that reports success/failure while checking nothing"), and it is invisible to every test in the file because no fixture ever names a module `buildSrc`.

answer_to_question: Yes -- two of the eleven still cannot separate the mutation they exist to guard against, both in coverage.py rather than in the floor/exclusion logic already hardened this round: (1) pct()'s zero-total guard / missing-counter default, and (2) the buildSrc module-discovery exclusion. Neither is hit by any of the eleven report()/module() fixtures, all of which use a single top-level 'format' module with both counters always present and non-zero.
